summary: A maintainer transfer enabled a malicious dependency to be added to the event-stream npm package dependency tree, targeting downstream cryptocurrency wallet software.

executive_summary.text: The event-stream incident turned a maintainer-transfer path into a malicious dependency insertion path for an npm package with downstream cryptocurrency-wallet exposure.
Threatpedia models this case as package publishing through the npm ecosystem, with event-stream and flatmap-stream preserved as separate package entities.

timeline.title: Dependency path changes before disclosure

timeline.title: Public issue documents the compromise

attack_chain.text: The incident began with a maintainer-transfer path that changed who could influence the package dependency tree.
The malicious package flatmap-stream entered the event-stream dependency path and became the payload-bearing component in the corpus model.
The corpus records credential and cryptocurrency-theft impact categories because the dependency path was tied to downstream wallet exposure.

affected_ecosystem.text: The affected ecosystem is npm, with event-stream as the trusted upstream package and flatmap-stream as the malicious dependency component.

defensive_lessons.text: High-impact package transfers should be treated as supply-chain events because maintainer authority can change dependency risk without changing the package name.
Dependency review should include newly introduced transitive packages, especially when a previously trusted package changes maintainership or dependency structure.

detection_notes.text: Useful detection pivots include the event-stream and flatmap-stream package names, npm registry publication paths, and dependency tree changes around the disclosure window.

open_questions.text: The corpus preserves the package and maintainer entities but does not expand this record into actor attribution.

notes: Maintainer transfer introduced flatmap-stream into the event-stream dependency path.
